pitch:
Fish Counting Machine Using Image Processing and Machine Learning

This project introduces an automated fish counting system designed for large-scale fish farms. Using image processing and machine learning, the system can accurately detect and count fish in real time, reducing human error and labour costs. It helps farmers monitor stock levels, plan feeding more efficiently, and manage harvest schedules. The system is adaptable to different fish species and farm environments, offering a cost-effective, scalable solution for modern aquaculture.

Smart Solar-Powered Water Pump with IoT Monitoring

One of the major challenges in agriculture is the lack of reliable and affordable irrigation systems, especially in rural areas with limited electricity access. My idea is to design a solar-powered water pump integrated with IoT technology that allows farmers to remotely monitor and control their irrigation.

The pump would be powered by renewable solar energy, making it eco-friendly and cost-effective. Through an IoT-enabled mobile app, farmers can track real-time data such as water flow rate, soil moisture, and energy usage. This eliminates water wastage, reduces energy costs, and ensures crops receive the right amount of water at the right time.

Unlike conventional pumps, this solution combines clean energy with smart monitoring. It is scalable, easy to maintain, and affordable for small-scale farmers. For the engineering community, it provides opportunities to integrate mechanical, electrical, and software engineering into a single impactful project.

The innovation lies in merging sustainability with digital technology to solve a real-world problem. By empowering farmers with data-driven decisions, this system can improve agricultural productivity, conserve resources, and contribute to food security in developing regions.

Smart Personal Health Record Tracker

The Smart Personal Health Record Tracker is a mobile application created to help individuals conveniently manage their health data in one secure place. Many people face challenges keeping track of scattered medical reports or remembering test follow-ups, which can delay early detection of health issues. This app solves that problem by allowing users to record essential test results, including lipid profile, fasting blood sugar (FBS), full blood count (FBC), blood pressure, and creatinine levels.

Once values are entered, the system automatically evaluates them against standard medical ranges and classifies results as Low, Normal, or High, offering instant feedback. Intuitive charts and trend lines visualize progress over time, making it easy to spot improvements or detect warning signs early. The app also includes personalized reminders for routine checkups or upcoming tests, ensuring users stay consistent with their health monitoring.

Unlike existing solutions that focus only on storage, this innovation combines record keeping with intelligent analysis and timely alerts. By giving users quick access to historical data, meaningful insights, and preventive guidance, the Smart Personal Health Record Tracker empowers individuals to take charge of their health, make informed lifestyle choices, and maintain stronger communication with healthcare professionals.

Smart Irrigation System for Paddy Cultivation

The system would use a network of IoT sensors deployed in paddy fields to collect real-time data on key parameters like soil moisture, temperature, and humidity. This data would be transmitted to a central platform for analysis. Using machine learning algorithms, the system would then predict the precise water requirements of the crops, factoring in weather forecasts and crop growth stages.
An automated control unit, integrated with the existing sluice gate infrastructure, would then precisely release the required amount of water, minimizing waste and optimizing irrigation schedules. A user-friendly mobile application would provide farmers with insights, alerts, and the ability to manually override the system, ensuring they have full control. This project would not only address water scarcity and inefficient usage but also reduce labor costs and increase rice yields, contributing to national food security and economic stability

I propose an AI-powered smart sorting system that uses computer vision and machine learning to classify and separate objects based on material, quality, or defects. Unlike traditional mechanical sorters, this system is low-cost, modular, and adaptable for industries such as recycling, agriculture, and food processing. It reduces manual labor, improves accuracy, and enhances efficiency. By integrating affordable embedded controllers like Raspberry Pi, it provides a scalable solution that benefits both industry and the engineering community as a practical platform for automation and research
